display_name: Hector Munro & Shah Alam II (Dual Character Sheet)
one_line: The Battle of Buxar commander and the Mughal emperor who granted the Company diwani rights after the Treaty of Allahabad.

appearance.age_look: Munro appears late 30s with a wiry, disciplined build; Shah Alam II appears early 40s with a dignified, slightly slender royal bearing.
appearance.face: Munro has a long, narrow face, light fair complexion, sharp nose, thin lips, faint crow’s-feet, and a default calm yet steely expression; Shah Alam II has an oval face, light brown North Indian complexion, neatly groomed beard and moustache, straight nose, kohl-lined eyes, and a serene, introspective gaze.
appearance.hair: Munro wears his light brown hair in tied-back 18th‑century officer’s style, rolled side curls above the ears, pulled into a short queue at the nape with a black ribbon, topped with a black bicorne hat edged in gold; Shah Alam II’s hair is covered by a tall, slightly conical Mughal turban of cream fabric with thin gold stripes, wrapped smoothly and adorned with a single central sarpech plume set with a red stone.
appearance.costume: Munro wears a mid‑18th‑century British East India Company officer’s uniform: a scarlet wool coat with long tails, white lapels and cuffs, gold braid edging and brass buttons, over a high‑collared white linen waistcoat and white cravat, with buff knee‑length breeches, white cotton stockings, and black leather shoes with small brass buckles; a black leather cross‑belt with a rectangular brass plate crosses his chest, and a plain brown leather waist belt holds his sword scabbard; Shah Alam II wears a full Mughal court jama of fine cream cotton patterned with subtle pale‑gold floral motifs, the wrap‑around robe crossing right over left and tied with a wide dark green silk patka sash at the waist, over loose white churidar trousers gathered at the ankles and simple brown leather mojari shoes; his upper body is further adorned with a sleeveless, light olive‑green silk over‑coat (char‑qab) that falls to mid‑thigh and is edged with narrow gold trim; jewellery is restrained but regal—one long pearl necklace with a central ruby pendant, a simple gold ring on his right hand, and small gold stud earrings.
appearance.signature: Munro carries a single polished steel officer’s sabre with a slightly curved blade and brass stirrup hilt in a plain black leather scabbard hanging from his belt, while Shah Alam II holds a rolled cream farman scroll tied with a dark green ribbon, symbolising the Treaty of Allahabad and the grant of diwani rights.

ref_desc: Hector Munro is a fair, sharp‑featured officer in a scarlet British uniform with white breeches, black bicorne hat, and brass‑hilted sabre, standing beside Shah Alam II, a light‑brown Mughal emperor in cream‑and‑gold jama, green sash, pearl necklace, and turban, holding a rolled cream farman scroll; their shared palette is scarlet, cream, gold, dark green, and black.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full‑body anime‑style model sheet of two standing figures side by side so they can be redrawn consistently: Hector Munro and Shah Alam II during 1764–1765 in North India. Munro is a late‑30s British East India Company officer with a long, narrow, fair face, sharp nose, thin lips, and calm steely eyes; his light brown hair is styled in 18th‑century fashion with rolled side curls and a short queue tied with a black ribbon, topped by a black bicorne hat edged in gold. He wears a scarlet long‑tailed wool officer’s coat with white lapels and cuffs, gold braid edging, and brass buttons over a high‑collared white waistcoat and white cravat, buff knee‑length breeches, white stockings, and black leather shoes with small brass buckles. A black leather cross‑belt with a brass plate runs over his chest, and a brown leather waist belt supports a plain black leather scabbard; his signature prop is a slightly curved polished steel officer’s sabre with a brass stirrup hilt, which he either rests his hand on or holds at his side. Next to him, Shah Alam II appears early‑40s with an oval, light brown North Indian face, straight nose, kohl‑lined expressive eyes, and a neatly groomed medium‑length beard and moustache, wearing a serene, dignified expression. His hair is covered by a tall, slightly conical Mughal turban made of cream fabric with fine gold stripes and a single central sarpech plume ornament set with a red stone. He is fully clothed in a cream cotton jama patterned with subtle pale‑gold floral motifs, the robe wrapping across the torso and tied with a wide dark green silk patka sash at the waist, over white churidar trousers gathered neatly at the ankles and brown leather mojari shoes; over the jama he wears a sleeveless light olive‑green silk over‑coat edged with narrow gold trim. His jewellery consists of a long pearl necklace with a central ruby pendant, a simple gold ring, and small gold stud earrings. His signature prop is a rolled cream farman scroll tied with a dark green ribbon, held carefully in one hand to symbolise the Treaty of Allahabad and the grant of diwani rights. Use a cohesive palette of scarlet red, cream, gold, dark green, and black; show both characters front and three‑quarter views in the same shot, making their facial features, hairstyles, clothing details, and signature props clearly visible for consistent redrawing.
